{{Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics}}

The '''men's 200 metre freestyle''' event at the [[2024 Summer Olympics]] was held on 28 and 29 July 2024 at [[Paris La Défense Arena]], which was converted to an [[Olympic-size swimming pool]] for the swimming events.

[[Romania at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Romanian]] [[David Popovici]] was considered by ''[[SwimSwam]]'' and ''[[Swimming World]]'' as the most likely to win the event, while [[Matt Richards (swimmer)|Matt Richards]] and [[Duncan Scott (swimmer)|Duncan Scott]] of [[Great Britain at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Great Britain]], [[Hwang Sun-woo]] of [[South Korea at the 2024 Summer Olympics|South Korea]], [[Danas Rapšys]] of [[Lithuania at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Lithuania]], [[Lukas Märtens]] of [[Germany at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Germany]] and the [[United States at the 2024 Summer Olympics|US]]' [[Luke Hobson]] were also possible contenders for medals. All except Hwang made it through to the final.

In the final, Märtens was in first place up until the final turn, when Hobson took the lead. Richards overtook him during the final length, and 195 metres into the race, Richards was in first, Hobson was in second and Popovici was in third. Over the final five metres Popovici overtook both to win gold with a time of 1:44.72, while Richards won silver with 1:44.74 and Hobson won bronze with 1:44.79. The 0.02 margin of victory was the smallest ever seen in this event at the Olympics, and Popovici's gold was the first Olympic medal for Romania since 2004.

== Background ==
[[Romania at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Romanian]] [[David Popovici]] won the event at the [[Swimming at the 2022 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 200 metre freestyle|2022 World Championships]], while [[Great Britain at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Great Britain]]'s [[Matt Richards (swimmer)|Matt Richards]] won it at the [[Swimming at the 2023 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 200 metre freestyle|2023 Championships]]. [[Duncan Scott (swimmer)|Duncan Scott]], also from Great Britain, won silver at the 2023 Championships. [[South Korea at the 2024 Summer Olympics|South Korea]]'s Hwang won the [[Swimming at the 2024 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 200 metre freestyle|2024 World Championships]], ahead of [[Lithuania at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Lithuania]]'s [[Danas Rapšys]] in second and the [[United States at the 2024 Summer Olympics|US]]' [[Luke Hobson]] in third.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Charlotte |date=23 July 2024 |title=2024 Olympics Previews: Baby Let the Games Begin (Men's 200 Free) (David's Version) |url=https://swimswam.com/2024-olympics-previews-baby-let-the-games-begin-mens-200-free-davids-version/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226035319/https://swimswam.com/2024-olympics-previews-baby-let-the-games-begin-mens-200-free-davids-version/ |archive-date=26 December 2024 |access-date=15 February 2025 |website=[[SwimSwam]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Great Britain's [[Tom Dean (swimmer)|Tom Dean]] won the event at the previous Olympics, but since each competing nation was only allowed to enter two athletes, and Richards and Scott had been chosen to swim instead of him, he did not compete.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Charlesworth |first=David |date=30 July 2024 |title=Great Britain Quartet Retain 4X200m Relay Title to Give GB First Paris Pool Gold |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/team-gb-tom-dean-duncan-scott-james-guy-adam-peaty-b2588737.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250213054807/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/olympics/team-gb-tom-dean-duncan-scott-james-guy-adam-peaty-b2588737.html |archive-date=13 February 2025 |access-date=15 February 2025 |website=[[The Independent]] |language=en}}</ref> Popovici won the [[Swimming at the 2024 European Aquatics Championships – Men's 200 metre freestyle|2024 European Championships]] with a time of 1:43.13, which was the fastest qualifying time ahead of [[Germany at the 2024 Summer Olympics|German]] [[Lukas Märtens]]' time of 1:44.14.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":12" /> Both ''[[SwimSwam]]'' and ''[[Swimming World]]'' predicted Popovici would win the event.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rieder |first=David |date=22 July 2024 |title=Olympic Swimming Predictions, Day 3: Summer Mcintosh, David Popovici to Claim Gold Medals |url=https://www.swimmingworldmagazine.com/news/olympic-swimming-predictions-day-3-summer-mcintosh-david-popovici-to-claim-gold-medals/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226155611/https://www.swimmingworldmagazine.com/news/olympic-swimming-predictions-day-3-summer-mcintosh-david-popovici-to-claim-gold-medals/ |archive-date=26 December 2024 |access-date=15 February 2025 |website=[[Swimming World]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

Prior to the event, the [[List of world records in swimming|world record]] was 1:42.00, set by [[Paul Biedermann]] of Germany in [[Swimming at the 2009 World Aquatics Championships – Men's 200 metre freestyle|2009]]. The [[List of Olympic records in swimming|Olympic record]] was 1:42.96, set by [[Michael Phelps]] of the US in [[Swimming at the 2008 Summer Olympics – Men's 200 metre freestyle|2008]].<ref name=":0"/>

The event was held at [[Paris La Défense Arena]], which was converted to a swimming pool for the swimming events.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Burgaud |first=Florian |date=22 July 2024 |title=From Concert Hall and Rugby Stadium to Olympic Swimming Pool Arena in a Matter of Weeks, The Metamorphosis of the Paris La Défense Arena Is Complete |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/concert-hall-rugby-stadium-olympic-swimming-pool-arena-paris-la-defense |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240804191900/https://olympics.com/en/news/concert-hall-rugby-stadium-olympic-swimming-pool-arena-paris-la-defense |archive-date=4 August 2024 |access-date=1 February 2025 |website=olympics.com |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC)}}</ref>

== Qualification ==
{{Further information|Swimming at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Qualification}}Each [[National Olympic Committee]] (NOC) was permitted to enter a maximum of two qualified athletes in each individual event, but only if both of them had attained the Olympic Qualifying Time (OQT).<ref name="swimming qual standards22">{{cite web |date=5 April 2022 |title=Paris 2024 – Swimming Info |url=https://www.fina.org/news/2563896/paris-2024-swimming-info |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230208222726/https://www.fina.org/news/2563896/paris-2024-swimming-info |archive-date=8 February 2023 |access-date=12 November 2022 |publisher=[[World Aquatics]]}}</ref> For this event, the OQT was 1:46.26. [[World Aquatics]] then considered athletes qualifying through universality; NOCs were given one event entry for each gender, which could be used by any athlete regardless of qualification time, providing the spaces had not already been taken by athletes from that nation who had achieved the OQT.<ref name="swimming qual standards22" /><ref name=":12">{{Citation |title=Entries List - Swimming |url=https://resources.fina.org/fina/document/2024/07/12/64c5ea6d-ef1b-49fc-a9cf-445966773ae7/OG00459_Swimming_entries_10.07.24.xlsx |access-date=18 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240712132646/https://resources.fina.org/fina/document/2024/07/12/64c5ea6d-ef1b-49fc-a9cf-445966773ae7/OG00459_Swimming_entries_10.07.24.xlsx |archive-date=12 July 2024 |url-status=live |publisher=[[World Aquatics]]}}</ref> Finally, the rest of the spaces were filled by athletes who had met the Olympic Consideration Time (OCT), which was 1:46.79 for this event.<ref name="swimming qual standards22" /> In total, 21 athletes qualified through achieving the OQT, four athletes qualified through universality places and three athletes qualified through achieving the OCT.<ref name=":12" />

== Heats ==
Four heats (preliminary rounds) took place on 28 July 2024, starting at 11:00.<ref name=":53" />{{Efn|All times are [[Central European Summer Time]] (UTC+2)}} The swimmers with the best 16 times in the heats advanced to the semifinals.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |date=24 July 2024 |title=Olympic Swimming Rules: How Can Swimmers Qualify for Finals and Win Medals - Format Explained |url=https://www.olympics.com/en/news/olympics-swimming-rules |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240821105532/https://olympics.com/en/news/olympics-swimming-rules |archive-date=21 August 2024 |access-date=7 May 2024 |website=olympics.com |publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC)}}</ref> Popovici led heat four from beginning to end to finish with the fastest qualifying time of 1:45.65, while Rapšys won heat three with the second fastest qualifying time of 1:45.91.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosado |first=Laura |date=28 July 2024 |title=2024 Paris Olympics: Day 2 Prelims Live Recap |url=https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-day-2-prelims-live-recap/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241223094631/https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-day-2-prelims-live-recap/ |archive-date=23 December 2024 |access-date=17 February 2025 |website=[[SwimSwam]] |language=en-US}}</ref> [[Belgium at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Belgian]] [[Lucas Henveaux]] swam a [[List of Belgian records in swimming|national record]] of 1:46.04 to qualify third.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Bush |first=Bradley |date=28 July 2024 |title=2024 Paris Olympics Data Dive (Day 2 Prelims) |url=https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-data-dive-day-2-prelims/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240907105142/https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-data-dive-day-2-prelims/ |archive-date=7 September 2024 |access-date=17 February 2025 |website=[[SwimSwam]] |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":53" />

== Semifinals ==
Two semifinals took place on 28 July, starting at 20:46.<ref name=":532" /> The swimmers with the best eight times in the semifinals advanced to the final.<ref name=":4" /> Popovici led from beginning to end to win the second semifinal with the fastest qualifying time of 1:44.53, while Scott finished behind him with the second fastest qualifying time of 1:44.94. Hobson won the first semifinal with 1:45.19, which was the third fastest qualifying time. Hobson, Märtens, [[Australia at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Australian]] [[Maximillian Giuliani]], Rapšys, Richards and [[Japan at the 2024 Summer Olympics|Japan]]'s [[Katsuhiro Matsumoto]] also qualified.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rosado |first=Laura |date=29 July 2024 |title=2024 Paris Olympics: Day 2 Finals Live Recap |url=https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-day-2-finals-live-recap/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226133054/https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-day-2-finals-live-recap/ |archive-date=26 December 2024 |access-date=17 February 2025 |website=[[SwimSwam]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Hwang did not qualify.<ref name=":532" />

== Final ==
The final took place at 20:41 on 29 July.<ref name=":533" /> After Richards had the fastest start, Märtens overtook him and retained the lead up until the 150 metre mark, which was three quarters of the way through the race. ''SwimSwam'' later opined that Märtens lost his chance at a medal due to his slow last [[tumble turn]] and [[Dolphin kick|underwater]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Hérailh |first=Dominique |date=3 September 2024 |title=How David Popovici Won 200 Free Olympic Gold in the Last Five Meters |url=https://swimswam.com/how-david-popovici-won-200-free-olympic-gold-in-the-last-five-meters/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227120556/https://swimswam.com/how-david-popovici-won-200-free-olympic-gold-in-the-last-five-meters/ |archive-date=27 December 2024 |access-date=17 February 2025 |website=[[SwimSwam]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

At 165 metres, Hobson had taken the lead, but by 175 metres Richards was first. At the 195 metre mark Richards was first, Hobson was second and Popovici was third.<ref name=":1" /> In what ''SwimSwam'' called a "wild finish", Popovici won gold with a time of 1:44.72, 0.02 seconds ahead of Richards in second, who in turn was 0.05 seconds ahead of Hobson, who came third.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Penland |first=Spencer |date=29 July 2024 |title=2024 Paris Olympics: Day 3 Finals Live Recap |url=https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-day-3-finals-live-recap/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250115083444/https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-day-3-finals-live-recap/ |archive-date=15 January 2025 |access-date=17 February 2025 |website=[[SwimSwam]] |language=en-US}}</ref> The 0.02 margin of victory was the smallest ever seen in this event at the Olympics.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=Bush |first=Bradley |date=29 July 2024 |title=2024 Paris Olympics Finals Day 3: Fun Facts |url=https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-finals-day-3-fun-facts/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240814033828/https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-olympics-finals-day-3-fun-facts/ |archive-date=14 August 2024 |access-date=17 February 2025 |website=[[SwimSwam]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

During the race, Hobson had the fastest tumble turns and underwaters, while Popovici swam the fastest during the [[front crawl]] sections.<ref name=":1" /> Popovici's gold was the first Olympic swimming medal for Romania since 2004,<ref name=":2" /> and after the race he called winning a "dream come true", adding, "I don't know how to describe it. It's so simple, yet so beautiful."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaufman |first=Sophie |date=30 July 2024 |title=2024 Paris, Euro Recap: European Men Have Won Every Individual Event Through Three Days |url=https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-euro-recap-european-men-have-won-every-individual-event-through-three-days/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241225203903/https://swimswam.com/2024-paris-euro-recap-european-men-have-won-every-individual-event-through-three-days/ |archive-date=25 December 2024 |access-date=17 February 2025 |website=[[SwimSwam]] |language=en-US}}</ref>
